description: Classical antiquity on a drowned coast. Olive country, marble hills and a sea between every two places; oil, wine and tribute rather than coin.

appearance.potter: Wet to the elbow, and turning something that will not be interrupted.
appearance.dyer: Purple to the second knuckle, and it does not wash off between seasons.
appearance.olive-presser: Standing on the beam because his own weight is part of the machine.
appearance.shipwright: Sighting down a plank with one eye shut, ignoring you entirely.
appearance.netmender: Mending, with the work hooked over one bare toe.
appearance.sponge-diver: Salt-dried, short of breath, and younger than the scars suggest.
appearance.archon: Seated, unhurried, and letting the silence do the asking.
appearance.herald: Out of breath and pretending otherwise.
appearance.oarsman: Hands like tackle, and sat down the moment he was allowed to.
appearance.priestess: Barefoot on cold stone, and unbothered by it.
appearance.stonecutter: White to the eyebrows, deaf on the side nearest the work.
appearance.vintner: Tastes, spits, and looks at you as though you had asked something rude.
appearance.bronzesmith: Green-stained at the cuff, weighing scrap that used to be a votive.

talksAbout.archon: the tribute, the ships that owe it, and the ones that will not come
talksAbout.priestess: the offerings, the season, and what the sea has not returned
talksAbout.oarsman: the crossing, the wind, and who is short a rower
talksAbout.sponge-diver: the deep ground off the point, and what else is down there
talksAbout.shipwright: keels, and the timber nobody can get any more
talksAbout.dyer: the price of purple, and the smell, which he cannot smell
talksAbout.herald: what was announced in the last three harbours

lore.title: The Long Crossing
lore.premise: The tribute ships are three seasons late and the harbours have begun quietly arming. Something is taking them between the islands, and nobody who has seen it has come back to be asked about it.
lore.era: the last summers of the old harbour league
lore.tone: bright, dry, and about to become political
deities: the Lady of the Threshing Floor

ambient: The light comes off the water and up under everything.
Cicadas, and then all of them stopping at once.
There is thyme crushed underfoot, and the smell arrives before you notice why.
A sail on the strait, too far out to be going anywhere near here.
The stone holds the heat long after the sun has gone off it.

warehouse: Sealed with pitch and stamped at the shoulder.
Purple, and the dye is worth more than the wool.
Come a very long way to be here.
hall: A prize for something, awarded to somebody now dead.
Resinated, and older than it should be.
temple: Terracotta, sooted at the lip, still half full.
smithy: Traded up the coast, and hoarded.
Somebody's offering, and now somebody's stock.
shop: Black figures on red. One of a pair, once.
Wound tight and kept out of the light.
house: A dozen of them, all differently chipped.
Pressed into a cake and wrapped in leaves.
mill: Sealed with pitch and stamped at the shoulder.
Bruised, and destined for the beam.
ruin: Owls on one face, a mint nobody here uses.
Six letters of a name, and the rest gone.

shop: First pressing, and the seller says so twice.
Pressed, wrapped, and good for a week on the road.
Black figures on red. Chipped at the foot.
Terracotta, and it comes with a thumb of oil in it.
Twisted flax, sold by the arm-span.
smithy: Softer than iron and holds an edge better than it should.
For a boat, a door, or an argument.
A dozen, barbed, on a twist of line.
Bronze tipped, and worn smooth at the grip.
press: Sealed at the shoulder and heavy as a child.
It tastes of the jar, which is the point.
In brine, in a stoppered pot.
inn: Three parts to one, and they mixed it in front of you.
A roof, a mat, and the harbour noise all night.
warehouse: Packed in layers, and it announces itself.
Heavy linen, sold by the ell.

bush: Grey-green, and it releases in the hand.
Prised out of a wall, which is where they prefer to be.
flowers: Three threads apiece, and worth the stooping.
forestFloor: Bitter as they are, which is very.
Dry twigs, gathered by the handful.
rock: It takes a hard edge and a harder spark.
Somebody was working here, a long time ago.
sand: Purple in the lip, and worth more than the fish it held.
tallGrass: Whatever was worth taking from a hand's width of hillside.
